categories.main_business_segments: Texas Roadhouse, Inc. operates three primary restaurant concepts: Texas Roadhouse (moderately priced, full-service, casual dining focused on steaks and American fare), Bubba’s 33 (full-service, casual dining with burgers, pizza, and sports bar atmosphere), and Jaggers (fast-casual, focused on burgers, chicken, and salads). The company manages its operations by concept, with Texas Roadhouse and Bubba’s 33 as reportable segments, and Jaggers and retail initiatives grouped under 'Other.' As of December 31, 2024, the company operated 666 company-owned restaurants and franchised 118 additional locations.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: The company emphasizes freshly prepared, high-quality food using proprietary recipes and hand-cut steaks prepared daily on-site. Food safety and consistency are maintained through rigorous training, product coaches, and technology such as digital kitchen display systems, electronic checklists, and digital temperature monitoring. Jaggers leverages fast-casual service models with drive-thru, carry-out, and dine-in options, while all concepts utilize modern information systems for operations, guest experience, and cybersecurity.
categories.primary_customers_markets: Texas Roadhouse targets a broad segment of consumers seeking affordable, high-quality casual dining, with a focus on families and groups. Bubba’s 33 appeals to sports fans and casual diners looking for a lively atmosphere, while Jaggers targets guests seeking quick, high-quality meals. The company serves both dine-in and to-go customers, with a growing emphasis on digital ordering and delivery, and also operates in both domestic and select international markets.
categories.geographic_coverage: As of year-end 2024, Texas Roadhouse, Inc. had a presence in 49 U.S. states, one U.S. territory, and ten foreign countries, with the majority of restaurants located in the United States. Key states include Texas and Florida, which together account for a significant portion of company-owned units. Internationally, the company has franchise operations in countries such as the Philippines, South Korea, Taiwan, Saudi Arabia, and Mexico.
categories.supply_chain_position: The company operates at the downstream end of the supply chain as a restaurant operator and franchisor, serving end consumers directly. It manages procurement of food and supplies, negotiates directly with suppliers, and works with national distributors for delivery to restaurants. Texas Roadhouse emphasizes long-term supplier relationships and supply chain resiliency but does not engage in upstream food production.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: Strategic priorities include expanding the restaurant base domestically and internationally, maintaining and improving restaurant-level profitability, leveraging scalable infrastructure, and returning capital to shareholders. The company invests in digital guest experiences, kitchen efficiency, and supply chain innovation, while also developing new concepts (e.g., Jaggers) and retail initiatives. R&D efforts focus on menu innovation, operational efficiency, and technology enhancements to support growth and guest satisfaction.
categories.revenue_model: Revenue is primarily generated from restaurant food and beverage sales at company-owned locations. Additional revenue streams include franchise royalties and fees, retail product licensing, and administrative services provided to certain franchisees. The company also earns income from gift card breakage and management fees for services rendered to franchise restaurants.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: Texas Roadhouse competes in the highly competitive casual dining segment against national chains (e.g., Outback Steakhouse, LongHorn Steakhouse, Chili’s), local independent restaurants, fast-casual and quick-service chains, and meal kit/grocery alternatives. The company positions itself as a value leader with a focus on quality, service, and a unique guest experience, and has outperformed industry indices in shareholder returns over the past five years.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: In 2024, Texas Roadhouse, Inc. generated $5.4 billion in total revenue, up 16% from the prior year, with net income of $433.6 million (a 42% increase). The company opened 31 new company restaurants and 14 franchise locations in 2024, with comparable restaurant sales growth of 8.5%. The company maintains a strong balance sheet, significant cash flow from operations, and a history of dividend growth and share repurchases.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: Texas Roadhouse emphasizes 'Legendary Food, Legendary Service®' with a focus on freshly prepared, high-quality meals at attractive price points, generous portions, and a fun, welcoming atmosphere. Differentiators include hand-cut steaks, made-from-scratch sides, attentive service, local community engagement, and a people-first culture. The company’s owner-operator model and disciplined pricing strategy reinforce its reputation for value and guest loyalty.
